params.body:
Elixir's side of the gateway's policy log (abovebeyond-ai/control, `docs/working-set.md`): the next version is drafted here, a narrowing is signed here, and a widening goes to the owner.

- The configuration Elixir writes gains `policy_log`: Portal's URL for the log, the owner's token keys as `widen` and `#agent-elixir` as `narrow`, all from the DID document. Without a readable DID document or an operator key the block is left out, so a configuration written during an outage is never the one carried over.
- Every minute, in remote mode beside the drift check, Elixir reads the gateway's `GET /v1/policy`. Nothing more while the gateway reads no policy log (404). Otherwise it compares what it would write with what is served: equal clears the draft; narrower (`PolicyLog::narrower`, a port of `policy.Narrower` tested against every case of control's `policy/log_test.go`) is signed with Elixir's key and posted to Portal; anything else becomes a draft for the owner, with the change in plain sentences in Portal's own words for hands and kinds.
- A narrowing is signed only when the key on the box is the one the DID log names for `#agent-elixir`; otherwise it too goes to the owner, since a version the gateway refuses blocks every later one.
- The `controlGrants` report carries `policy: {version, hash}` from `/v1/agents`, so Portal knows what the gateway serves.

A narrowing signed by this code was checked with control's own `ParseVersion` and `Next`: parsed, and accepted from the narrow signer.

Tests: 719 pass (16 new: `ControlPolicyLogTest`, two in `ControlGrantsReportTest`). Pint and PHPStan pass.
params.title: Elixir drafts the gateway's next policy version, and signs a narrowing
